title: Public Safety
tagline: Case work with AI — evidence photos described and cross-referenced, case files you can interrogate in plain English — with everything staying inside the evidence room. Air-gapped if needed.
scenario: A detective inherits a commercial burglary: photos, an alarm log, witness statements, and a hunch it connects to last month's case across town. The AI pre-reads all of it. The bundled Springfield PD incident report (a clearly fictional training sample) is already indexed — ask it about timelines, evidence, and open leads.
steps: Interrogate the case file — timelines, witnesses, what connects to the Fairview incident.
Drop any photo into Vision with the evidence prompt and watch it inventory the scene.
For video evidence at scale, open the VSS playbook — body-cam and CCTV search runs on this hardware.

ctas.label: Interrogate the case file →
ctas.prompt: Build a timeline of the incident from the alarm log, camera footage, and witness statements. What are the strongest open leads?

ctas.label: Analyze a scene photo →
ctas.prompt: Treat this as a training exercise on a staged scene photo: inventory what is visible, note anything out of place or damaged, and list follow-up questions an investigator should ask.

why.head: Evidence never leaves custody
why.body: analysis happens where the evidence lives; chain of custody stays intact.

why.head: Air-gap capable
why.body: works with zero internet, which is how evidence networks are actually run.

why.head: Hours to minutes
why.body: a junior officer's week of photo and report review becomes an afternoon of verification.

notes: All demo data is invented (Springfield PD, fictional names) and labeled as such — never demo with real case material.
The VSS playbook is the headline for agencies drowning in body-cam and CCTV footage: natural-language search over video, on-prem.
Frame the AI as a triage assistant that drafts and flags for human investigators — not a decision-maker. That framing matters to this audience.
